cluster: Ursa Major (ucrslurmcl), UCR Research Computing, Google Cloud us-central1-a

partitions.name: computehigh
partitions.use_for: Intel Sapphire Rapids c3-highcpu-44, Tier_1 networking. Fastest per core; best for tightly coupled MPI (GROMACS, LAMMPS, CFD).

partitions.name: gpul4
partitions.use_for: One NVIDIA L4 (24 GB) per node. ML training/inference, GPU MD (GROMACS/LAMMPS/OpenMM -cuda builds), LLMs up to ~8B (fp16) or ~14B (4-bit).

partitions.name: highmem
partitions.use_for: n2-highmem-64 with ~496 GB RAM. Genome assembly, large in-memory analytics, big matrices.

partitions.name: nvmescratch
partitions.use_for: c2-standard-16 with 100 GB pd-ssd boot disk (no local NVMe despite the name). I/O-heavy staging.

partitions.name: spot
partitions.use_for: Same nodes as standard at about half price, but Google may reclaim a node with ~30 s notice. Use for job arrays, parameter sweeps and restartable work; add --requeue.

partitions.name: standard
partitions.use_for: Default. AMD EPYC Milan c2d-standard-32. General CPU work and MPI.

rules: Python: load exactly one Python environment module: python-sci (CPU science stack) or python-ml (PyTorch/GPU). There are no per-package Python modules (no py-numpy etc.) and no bare python module; for anything else use a Pixi/conda or uv environment inside the job.
Slurm CPUs are physical cores (ThreadsPerCore=1); never request more CPUs per node than the partition lists.
Nodes are created on demand: the first job on a cold partition waits ~90 s-5 min for boot.
Every job task gets a private $TMPDIR (/tmp/job-<id>-<user>, node-local) and shared $SCRATCH (/scratch/$USER, 2.5 TB, not backed up).
/home and /apps are shared NFS (Filestore) on every node.
Nodes have outbound internet through Cloud NAT (pip, conda, docker pulls, dataset downloads all work).
OS: Rocky Linux 8.10, glibc 2.28, system GCC 8.5; use module gcc/* for modern compilers.
Code built for AVX-512 crashes on the AMD standard/spot nodes; the site stack targets x86-64-v3 (AVX2).
Partitions are exclusive: a job gets whole nodes.

install_tools.name: uv
install_tools.use: uv venv $TMPDIR/v && . $TMPDIR/v/bin/activate && uv pip install <pkgs>; fastest way to get PyPI packages

install_tools.name: pixi
install_tools.use: conda-forge/bioconda environments without root: pixi init && pixi add <pkgs>

install_tools.name: apptainer
install_tools.use: apptainer pull x.sif docker://<image>; apptainer exec [--nv] x.sif <cmd>; unprivileged, /dev/fuse available

install_tools.name: spack
install_tools.use: compiled HPC codes; the shared stack is maintained by Research Computing

install_tools.name: pip (inside any env)
install_tools.use: wheels need LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$CONDA_PREFIX/lib inside Pixi/conda envs (Rocky 8 libstdc++ is old)

recipes.name: GROMACS (CPU, MPI)
recipes.notes: Use thread/rank counts with small prime factors (16, 20), not 22.

recipes.name: Scientific Python (site env, CPU)
recipes.notes: Python 3.12 with numpy scipy pandas matplotlib seaborn scikit-learn statsmodels sympy numba xarray netCDF4 h5py zarr dask polars pyarrow astropy astroquery skyfield sunpy cartopy geopandas rasterio networkx biopython pysam scikit-image opencv jupyterlab; cutadapt, multiqc, snakemake. Extra packages: uv venv --system-site-packages $TMPDIR/v. Every package is import-tested together. Do not combine with other Python modules.

recipes.name: PyTorch (site env, CUDA 12.4)
recipes.notes: Python 3.12, torch 2.5.1+cu124, numpy, scipy, pandas, scikit-learn, transformers, JupyterLab.

recipes.name: Current PyTorch (CUDA 13)
recipes.run: uv venv $TMPDIR/v && . $TMPDIR/v/bin/activate && uv pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130

recipes.name: Read mapping + variant calling
recipes.run: bwa mem -t $SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE ref.fa r1.fq r2.fq | samtools sort -o aln.bam; bcftools mpileup -f ref.fa aln.bam | bcftools call -mv

usage_cards.su2: SU2 8.2 (`module load openmpi su2/8.2.0`): binaries SU2_CFD, SU2_DEF, SU2_SOL. Incompressible cases: SOLVER= INC_NAVIER_STOKES with INC_* keys (not the compressible solver). OUTPUT_FILES= (RESTART, CSV) writes restart_flow.csv (PointID,x,y,Pressure,Velocity_x,Velocity_y,...); history.csv holds residuals. Mesh .su2 files: NDIME, NELEM, then NPOIN, then NMARK. mpirun -np N SU2_CFD case.cfg; give it </dev/null inside loops. SPECIFIED_INLET_PROFILE in an unsteady run reads <stem>_00000.dat (write it and <stem>.dat); format NMARK=/MARKER_TAG=/NROW=/NCOL=6 then x y T |U| nx ny. No VISC_NUM_METHOD_FLOW in 8.2.
usage_cards.gromacs: GROMACS 2026.1: gmx_mpi (openmpi build) and gmx; -cuda module for GPUs. Keep -ntomp x ranks free of large prime factors (22 cores: use 20 or 16), or domain decomposition aborts.
usage_cards.lammps: LAMMPS 20250722: executable lmp (openmpi build); lammps/...-cuda for GPUs with -sf gpu -pk gpu 1. Packages: KSPACE MANYBODY MISC MOLECULE REPLICA RIGID only (no GRANULAR/DEM, no fix pour). For granular work use conda-forge lammps=2023.08.02 (has GRANULAR, runs on glibc 2.28; newer conda-forge builds need glibc 2.29+).
usage_cards.python-sci: python-sci/2026.09: Python 3.12 with numpy, scipy, pandas, matplotlib, numba, xarray, astropy, skyfield, biopython, networkx, scikit-learn, statsmodels. Extra packages via pip in a venv layered on it. OR-Tools and other wheels bundling abseil/protobuf crash layered: use an isolated venv.
usage_cards.python-ml: python-ml/2026.09: PyTorch 2.5.1+cu124 (GPU-verified on L4), transformers, scikit-learn, numpy, scipy, pandas, matplotlib, networkx (no numba). It is a venv: layer extra packages with a .pth to its site-packages, not only --system-site-packages.
usage_cards.gcc: gcc/13.5.0 default (also 12.2.1, 14.4.0, 15.3.0, 16.2.0). -march=x86-64-v3 is safe on every partition.
usage_cards.openmpi: openmpi/5.0.10: launch with srun or mpirun -np $SLURM_NTASKS; MPI-built modules appear after loading it.
usage_cards.cp2k: CP2K 2026.2 (openmpi): cp2k.psmp; set OMP_NUM_THREADS and ranks so ranks*threads <= cores.
usage_cards.quantum-espresso: Quantum ESPRESSO 7.6 (openmpi): pw.x, ph.x; pseudopotentials must be downloaded into the job (e.g. SSSP from materialscloud) and pointed to with pseudo_dir.
usage_cards.apptainer: Apptainer 1.5 on compute nodes via `module load apptainer`; prebuilt images in /apps/containers (use in place, never `apptainer pull` a path); `apptainer exec --nv` for GPUs. The CUDA toolkit (nvcc) is in /apps/containers/cuda-12.4-devel.sif, not a module.
usage_cards.os: Compute nodes run Rocky Linux 8 (glibc 2.28). Recent conda-forge/pip binaries built for glibc 2.29+ fail with "GLIBC_2.xx not found": pin an older build, or use a module or container.

job_header.use: source it near the top of every job script (. /apps/docs/templates/job-header.sh): sets TMPDIR, SCRATCH, package caches, URSA_CONTAINERS; ursa_conda_libs fixes pip wheels inside Pixi/conda envs

how_to_load: module load <name>[/<version>]; MPI-built packages appear after `module load openmpi` (or mpich / intel-oneapi-mpi). Compilers: gcc/13.5.0 is the default toolchain of the Spack stack. `module spider <name>` shows how to reach any module.
